editorial_thesis: The important question is not whether a game is engaging. The question is whether the mechanic is doing causal therapeutic work.

vid-hero-prescription-blocks.note: Strongest immediate hook; clean bottle-to-block transformation and excellent phone readability.

vid-memory-competition.note: Visually forceful representation of intrusive-memory competition; clearly editorial/illustrative.

vid-engagement-vs-efficacy.note: Clean controller/pathway metaphor; useful for causal-mechanism distinction and closing callback.

vid-software-repurposing.note: Concept works, but arcade styling is more generic/garish than intended; keep duration short.

img-dtx-metaphors/0.note: Clear prescription-game visual; strong graphic connective tissue.

img-dtx-metaphors/1.note: Good split-panel metaphor but busier composition.

img-latent-therapy/0.note: Strong discovery/lab atmosphere, although metaphor is abstract.

img-latent-therapy/2.note: Useful science-lab texture; not sufficiently literal for a hero beat.

img-host-world/0.note: Generated host identity is inconsistent with a canonical Satoshi character.

img-host-world/1.note: Same identity-consistency problem; no need for a host shot in voiceover-first edit.

img-memory-mechanism/0.note: Triptych layout feels like an infographic generated inside the image; Remotion should draw structured graphics instead.

img-memory-mechanism/1.note: Same issue: generated multi-panel science graphic is less credible than native overlays.

img-memory-mechanism/2.note: Same issue; retain only as emergency filler.

timeline.screen_text: A game mechanic can behave like an intervention.
Compete for the same cognitive machinery?
Tetris has been studied after trauma for intrusive memories.
timeline.instruction: Use native Remotion typography plus an authentic study/source receipt. Do not use generated imagery as evidence.

timeline.screen_text: What other mechanics are hiding in plain sight?

regeneration.rationale: The current library covers hook, mechanism, repurposing and callback. The weakest asset is software-repurposing, but it is acceptable as a brief 4-second bridge. Spend reserve only after a first Remotion cut exposes a specific weakness.
